headline: Why You Stop Using Planners: A Blank Thursday and a Book Under the Post
items: Monday to Wednesday are full: neat handwriting, colors, a plan for Thursday.

Friday you opened the book, saw the blank Thursday sitting there, and closed it.
It's now the following Tuesday and the book is under a pile of post.

headline: Choosing a Planner for ADHD: Five Checks to Run Before You Commit
sub: Whether it's paper or an app, run it past these before you commit.
items: It survives a missed week without extra work from you.
It doesn't count or display what you didn't do, so a gap is invisible.
It asks for very little to start, and you can be using it in five minutes.
You can put it down halfway and pick it up again where you stopped.
It's somewhere you'll pass without deciding to look.

headline: Stopped Using Your Planner? A More Useful Reading Than Lost Motivation
items: The easy reading is that you lost motivation.
A more useful one is that the book had a rule in it: every day gets an entry.
Once a day is blank, the rule is broken, and every page after that shows you the break.

headline: How to Restart a Half-Finished Project: A Four-Line Restart Note
sub: An illustration, not a real case. Say you started a warranty claim on a dishwasher six weeks ago and stopped.
items: Where did I get to? Form filled in to page 2. Receipt photographed but not attached.
Was anything missing? The serial number. It's on a sticker inside the door.
Smallest next piece: Open the door and photograph the serial number sticker.
Still needed? Yes. The claim window closes on the 30th.
